chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “For a woman, it is sufficient in wiping the head that she wipe its front part to the measure of three fingers, and she does not remove her head-covering from it.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثِ أَصَابِعَ: three fingers; the measure mentioned for the wiping area
key_terms.خِمَارَهَا: her head-covering; the garment she is not required to remove
key_terms.مَسْحِ: wiping; the prescribed act of masḥ in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.مُقَدَّمَهُ: its front part; the forepart of the head intended in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلرَّأْسِ: the head; the body part to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the subject of the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: How much of the head must a woman wipe in wudu (ablution), and must she remove her khimār?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman’s wudu (ablution), stating that wiping the front part of the head in the measure of three fingers is sufficient for masḥ. It also indicates that she is not required to remove her khimār in order to perform this wiping.
